theme: We are his people and the sheep of his pasture
readingInstruction: Read Psalm 100. It is a short psalm of thanksgiving, a call to the whole earth to come to the LORD with gladness. Read it aloud, as if you were entering the temple gates.
settingTheScene: Psalm 100 is titled “A Psalm for giving thanks.” It was probably sung by pilgrims as they entered the temple courts. It has a simple structure: two calls to worship (vv. 1 to 2 and 4), each followed by a reason (vv. 3 and 5). It has been sung for centuries by the church. It follows Psalm 23 with the same image of the flock.
observation: “Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth!” (v. 1).
“Know that the LORD, he is God!” (v. 3).
“It is he who made us, and we are his; we are his people, and the sheep of his pasture” (v. 3).
“Enter his gates with thanksgiving, and his courts with praise!” (v. 4).
“Give thanks to him; bless his name!” (v. 4).
“For the LORD is good; his steadfast love endures forever, and his faithfulness to all generations” (v. 5).
interpretation:
The psalm opens with a command to all the earth, not just Israel: make a joyful noise. Worship is not meant to be grim. “Serve the LORD with gladness! Come into his presence with singing!” Service and joy go together. The word for serve is the word for work or worship, and it is to be done gladly.

Then comes the foundation: “Know that the LORD, he is God!” All true worship begins with knowing who God is. He is the LORD, the covenant God. “It is he who made us, and we are his.” We did not make ourselves, and we belong to him. “We are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.” The shepherd image returns. We are not self-made or self-sufficient. We are creatures and sheep, cared for by the Maker.

The second call is to enter his gates with thanksgiving and his courts with praise. Gratitude is the doorway to worship. We come not because we have earned entry, but because we have been invited. “Give thanks to him; bless his name!”

And the second reason is a threefold description of God: “For the LORD is good; his steadfast love endures forever, and his faithfulness to all generations.” Good describes his nature. Steadfast love describes his covenant commitment. Faithfulness describes his reliability across generations. This does not change. The generations before us trusted this God, and the generations after us will be able to.

The psalm is the response of the redeemed. In Christ, the invitation to the nations is extended to the world, and the flock is gathered from all peoples. The sheep of his pasture are those who hear his voice. John 10 says there will be one flock and one shepherd.
connection: Psalm 95 is a similar call to worship. Psalm 117 invites all nations. Psalm 136 repeats “for his steadfast love endures forever.” Ezekiel 34:30-31 says the sheep are God’s people. Colossians 3:15-17 calls for thankfulness and singing. Hebrews 13:15 speaks of a sacrifice of praise. Revelation 7:9-12 pictures the nations praising God.
application:
Begin today with gladness. Give thanks for three things before you do anything else.

Sing a song of praise, or play one, and sing along.

Thank God for his faithfulness to your family, in the past and now.
prayerPrompts: Make a joyful noise to God, in your own words.
Thank him that you are his people and the sheep of his pasture.
